In an in-depth interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop application and discussed plans for a future tab-less interface. The full interview can be viewed below.

In the future, users will be able to seamlessly complete various tasks within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern premiered a preview clip of her exclusive interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her brand new YouTube channel "New Things."

Stern released the full interview today, covering the new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware development plans, the lawsuit with Apple, and the recent data leak incident on Hugging Face.

During the interview, Stern pointed out that OpenAI had previously decided to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop applications and launch a brand new agent mode called Work.

The merged interface caused considerable confusion, especially for users who just wanted to continue using ChatGPT but had difficulty finding their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the application, adding separate "Work" and "Chat" tabs at the top of the interface and introducing a dropdown menu in the sidebar to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. Although it is no longer as difficult as before, the interface is still somewhat complex.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's description of the new interface as "a bit messy" and added that this is only a "transitional arrangement" toward the future, where the "Work" tab will eventually disappear and its functions will be "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also stated that despite the confusing rollout of the merged application, OpenAI still achieved the expected results, with the number of Codex users soaring from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth was purely due to forcibly bundling Codex into the ChatGPT application, Brockman acknowledged this again but argued that to a certain extent, this was also part of the plan:

The entire interview is excellent and definitely worth watching. The program also features a very Joanna Stern-style segment where she attempts to bring ChatGPT voice features into the conversation—and the results are exactly what you would expect.
